newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends bit firmer after BOJ Matsushita.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends bit firmer after BOJ Matsushita.

text.p: Key March three-month Euroyen interest rate futures closed slightly firmer on Friday after Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita's comments on economic recovery remained the same as previous comments.

Those who sold this morning on worries over a possible U.S. rate hike covered their shorts in the afternoon after Matsushita's comments. A fall in Tokyo stocks also lent support to the market, traders said.
"For our nation's economy to move on to a self-sustained recovery track, the current recovery needs to gain more strength," Matsushita said.

Earlier, the March was sold on expectations that the U.S. August jobs data due later on Friday may be stronger than expected and may provide a reason for the Fed to raise interest rates, traders said.
But sentiment improved by early afternoon after the key contract's trial below a support of 99.01 failed, they said.
The contract ended at 99.06 after moving between 99.02 and 99.06 in turnover of 52,828 contracts.

"If the U.S. jobs data is strong, we should draw a totally different picture," said a city bank dealer. A tightening by the Fed may result in the yen's fall against the dollar and dampen Euroyen futures because Japan is unlikely to take a similar step for the time being, traders said.

The key overnight call rate dropped to 0.42-0.43 percent from Thursday's weighted average of 0.47 because fund suppliers were eager to lower the rate amid a lack of demand for funds by banks. "Today's BOJ operation showed how weak banks' fund demand was even for such funds maturing after the current bank reserve reporting period," said another city bank dealer.

The BOJ's buying offer of 300 billion yen in bills maturing on September 17 failed to collect enough bids. This showed banks' lack of appetite for funds covering the end of the current reserve period on September 13, traders said.

The fall in the key rate was also attributed to an easing of upward pressure in the long end of the market. Banks have raised sufficient funds covering the fiscal half-year book closings by issuing certificates of deposit since August, traders said. Some 230 billion yen of one-month CDs were issued at 0.53 percent on Friday.
